summary: This week's Gulf agenda was dominated by the physical and institutional build-out of AI. Abu Dhabi's 5-gigawatt UAE–US AI campus was reported on schedule despite regional tension, even as AI-driven demand pushed storage prices higher — a reminder that sovereign AI ambition carries a real infrastructure-cost tail. In banking, modernisation accelerated: Commercial Bank of Dubai became the first UAE bank to enable in-app payments from other banks, a concrete open-banking milestone, while Oman moved to regulate investment banking and DIFC spotlighted challenger-bank disruption. Government digitisation remained the region's steadiest demand engine — from smart services for Two Holy Mosques visitors and Kuwait's hyperscaler cloud programmes to the UAE's tourist VAT-refund network surpassing 19,300 outlets and a second trial of an autonomous patrol boat in Abu Dhabi. Saudi Arabia widened its AI base through Monsha'at–SDAIA programmes. Markets were resilient: most Gulf bourses gained despite stalled Iran talks and Hormuz shipping disruption. For executives, the throughline is convergence — AI, payments, and public-sector platforms are maturing together, raising both the opportunity and the cost of moving too slowly.

stories.t: Abu Dhabi's 5GW UAE–US AI campus stays on schedule
stories.b: Abu Dhabi's planned 5-gigawatt AI campus, developed with US partners, is reported to remain on track despite regional conflict. It is positioned as one of the largest AI compute build-outs in the region.
stories.w: Sovereign-scale compute is becoming a strategic asset. Its continuation through geopolitical stress signals the UAE's intent to anchor regional AI capacity — with implications for data residency, partnerships, and where GCC institutions run large-model workloads.

stories.t: CBD becomes first UAE bank to accept in-app payments from other banks
stories.b: Commercial Bank of Dubai says it is the first UAE bank to let customers make payments from accounts held at other banks directly within its mobile app.
stories.w: A concrete step toward open banking in the UAE. Cross-bank initiation shifts the competitive battleground to the app layer and pressures peers to accelerate account-aggregation and payment-initiation roadmaps.

stories.t: Oman moves to regulate investment banking activities
stories.b: Oman has introduced regulation governing investment banking activities, formalising oversight of the segment.
stories.w: Clearer rules can deepen Oman's capital markets and attract advisory and underwriting activity, but they also raise compliance requirements for banks operating cross-border in the GCC.

stories.t: Monsha'at and SDAIA conclude national AI Week
stories.b: Saudi Arabia's SME authority Monsha'at and the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA) concluded a national AI Week programme aimed at accelerating AI adoption, including among smaller enterprises.
stories.w: State-backed AI capacity-building widens the adoption base and talent pool; institutions should expect rising AI fluency among partners, suppliers, and SME customers in the Saudi market.

stories.t: Kuwait's CAIT reviews Google Cloud and Microsoft transformation projects
stories.b: Kuwait's Central Agency for Information Technology reviewed digital transformation projects with Google Cloud and Microsoft.
stories.w: Hyperscaler-led government programmes signal continued public-sector cloud migration in Kuwait — relevant to vendors, integrators, and any institution planning sovereign-cloud or data-localisation strategies.

stories.t: Smart digital services expand for Two Holy Mosques visitors
stories.b: Saudi authorities highlighted expanded smart digital services to improve the experience of visitors to the Two Holy Mosques.
stories.w: Delivering digital services at pilgrimage scale is a demanding proving ground; the identity, crowd and payment capabilities built here often set the bar for national gov-tech.

stories.t: AI-driven demand fuels SSD shortage, pushing storage prices up
stories.b: Surging AI workloads are being linked to a shortage of solid-state storage, sending prices higher.
stories.w: AI ambition carries a hardware-cost tail. Rising storage and memory prices will pressure infrastructure budgets and total cost of ownership for data-heavy AI programmes.

stories.t: DIFC: challenger banks are redefining banking innovation
stories.b: A DIFC piece examines how challenger banks are reshaping banking innovation and customer expectations.
stories.w: Digital-first entrants continue to reset the pace on onboarding, UX and product velocity — a competitive signal for incumbent GCC banks weighing build-versus-partner strategies.

stories.t: Abu Dhabi runs second field trial of autonomous patrol boat
stories.b: Under the Smart and Autonomous Systems Council, Abu Dhabi's Integrated Transport Centre conducted a second field trial of an autonomous patrol boat with maritime partners.
stories.w: Autonomous systems are moving from pilots toward operations in the UAE public sector; maritime and mobility use-cases point to procurement and governance frameworks worth tracking.

stories.t: UAE digital tourist VAT-refund network tops 19,300 outlets
stories.b: The UAE's digital tourist VAT refund system is now connected to more than 19,300 retail outlets, according to the Federal Tax Authority.
stories.w: Digitised tax rails at retail scale improve compliance and traveller experience and create data and integration opportunities for banks, PSPs and retail-tech providers.

themes.t: Sovereign AI: from ambition to infrastructure
themes.b: The region's AI story shifted from strategy to build-out — Abu Dhabi's 5GW campus, Saudi AI Week, and government AI programmes — while an AI-driven storage shortage exposed the rising hardware cost behind the ambition.

CBD's cross-bank in-app payments, Oman's new investment-banking rules, and DIFC's challenger-bank commentary all point to a more competitive, more regulated, more digital banking market across the GCC.

themes.t: Government service delivery goes digital and autonomous
themes.b: From smart services for Two Holy Mosques visitors and Kuwait's hyperscaler cloud programmes to the UAE's VAT-refund rails and autonomous maritime trials, public-sector platforms remain the region's most consistent transformation engine.

items: Pressure-test infrastructure budgets against rising storage and memory prices before scaling AI workloads.
Revisit sovereign-cloud and data-residency options as hyperscaler government programmes expand across the GCC.
Prioritise API and payment-initiation readiness as open banking gains ground in the UAE.
Extend security and governance frameworks to autonomous and AI systems moving from pilot to production.
Reassess third-party and data-sharing risk as cross-bank payment and aggregation features widen.
Align controls with tightening regional regulation, such as Oman's investment-banking oversight.
Position data platforms for open-banking data flows and account-aggregation use-cases.
Stand up governance for AI training and inference data as national AI programmes raise expectations.
Treat digitised government rails (VAT refund, smart services) as new external data sources.
Benchmark digital onboarding and UX against challenger-bank standards.
Build partnerships with national AI authorities and SME programmes to access talent and pilots.
Sequence AI initiatives with realistic infrastructure cost and capacity assumptions.

market.b: Regional compute build-out continued (Abu Dhabi's 5GW campus) even as AI-driven storage shortages pushed hardware prices up — capacity is expanding, but input costs are rising.
Momentum across KSA (Holy Mosques smart services, Tabuk hackathon) and Kuwait (hyperscaler cloud programmes); public-sector digitisation remains the region's most consistent demand engine.
Open-banking moves (CBD cross-bank payments) and new Omani investment-banking rules point to a modernising, more contested banking market.
Most Gulf bourses gained despite stalled Iran talks and Hormuz shipping disruption, showing continued investor resilience to geopolitical noise.
Global signals — Gemini passing one billion users — underscore the pace institutions must match in their own AI roadmaps.

ceo.lead: If I were advising the CEO of a Gulf bank or government technology organisation, the three issues I would put on the leadership agenda this week are:
items: AI is now an infrastructure and cost question, not only a capability one — secure compute and budget for a rising hardware tail.
Open banking has arrived in practice; decide quickly whether to lead, partner, or defend on cross-bank payments.
Regional stability held and markets shrugged off Hormuz disruption — but geopolitical and concentration risk still belong on the board agenda.
